core_obligations: Main proof (proof lines 5156-5175): for an inverse system (K_n) the author computes R lim K_n through the defining product and shift, applies Rf_* to that presentation, and uses that Rf_* commutes with products in the derived setting, which gives the identification with R lim Rf_*K_n.

Alternate proof (proof lines 5178-5198): when the site has enough points, the same statement is proved by checking on stalks through the defining distinguished triangle of the derived limit, since the pushforward is computed pointwise in that case.
proof_roadmap: Present the derived limit by its defining product and shift.
Apply the derived pushforward and use its compatibility with products.
Identify the result with the derived limit of the pushed-forward system; alternatively check on stalks when points exist.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the derived pushforward commutes with derived limits: Rf_*R lim K_n = R lim Rf_*K_n for an inverse system of objects of the derived category (statement lines 5149-5154). The main proof presents the derived limit through its defining product and shift, applies Rf_* and uses its compatibility with products (proof lines 5156-5175). The author then adds an alternate proof in the case where the site has enough points, checking the statement on stalks via the distinguished triangle defining the derived limit (proof lines 5178-5198). The non-formal content is the compatibility of the derived pushforward with products. The claim is H2: one argument with an alternative given by the author.
